en: Jose Rizal wrote the novel Noli Me Tangere to expose the abuses of the Spanish friars in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, known as the monkey-eating eagle, is the national bird and a critically endangered species.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines holds the judicial power to interpret the laws and settle actual controversies.
Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces by carving the mountains of Ifugao over 2,000 years ago.
The Barasoain Church in Malolos, Bulacan, served as the site of the first Philippine Congress in 1898.
Fe del Mundo became the first Asian to study at Harvard Medical School and invented a bamboo incubator.
The Ati-Atihan festival in Kalibo, Aklan, honors the Santo Niño with dancers painting their bodies with black soot.
The 1987 Philippine Constitution guarantees the right to suffrage, allowing citizens aged eighteen and above to vote.
Baybayin is an ancient Philippine writing system used by early Filipinos to write Tagalog before the Spanish arrived.
Guillermo Tolentino sculpted the Oblation, the official symbol of the University of the Philippines, representing selfless sacrifice.
Lapu-Lapu defeated Ferdinand Magellan in the Battle of Mactan on April 27, 1521, defending his native territory.
